h: שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, מַאֲמָר י׳ Shabbos HaGadol — Maamar Yud

p: הַטַּעַם שֶׁקּוֹרִין לְשַׁבָּת זֶה שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל
As to the reason why this Shabbos is called Shabbos HaGadol,
כָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת
Tosafos wrote
(שַׁבָּת פ"ז: דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל וְאוֹתוֹ)
(Shabbos 87b, s.v. V'oso)
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָז חָל עָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ בְּשַׁבָּת וְנַעֲשָׂה בּוֹ נֵס גָּדוֹל,
that it is because then the tenth of the month fell on Shabbos and a great miracle occurred on it;
וּכְבָר הִקְשׁוּ עַל זֶה דְּהָיָה לִקְרוֹת לְעָשׂוֹר בַּחֹדֶשׁ יוֹם הַגָּדוֹל.
and commentators have already asked on this that they should have called the tenth of the month "the Great Day."
הָעִנְיָן: שֶׁכְּבָר אָמַרְנוּ בְּטַעַם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ פָּרָשַׁת הַפֶּסַח,
The explanation is: we have already discussed the reason why the section of the Pesach offering was spoken on Rosh Chodesh,
אַף שֶׁמִּקָּחוֹ מִבְּעָשׂוֹר
even though its acquisition was from the tenth
רַק שֶׁאָז זָכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִקְדוּשָּׁה חֲדָשָׁה,
because then Israel merited a new holiness,
שֶׁהוּא לִזְכּוֹת לֶאֱכוֹל אֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל בֶּן נֹחַ לִזְכּוֹת.
which is to merit eating in holiness, something a descendant of Noach cannot attain.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
And this is what is said
(שְׁמוֹת י"ב, ב'):
(Shemos 12:2):
הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים,
"This month shall be unto you the head of months"
וְנִצְטַוּוּ מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן לְקַדְּשׁוֹ,
and Moshe and Aharon were commanded to sanctify it,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יַכְנִיסוּ קְדוּשָּׁה זוֹ בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and through this they would bring this holiness into all of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
as they said
(רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ"ד.):
(Rosh Hashanah 24a):
רֹאשׁ בֵּית דִּין אוֹמֵר מְקוּדָּשׁ וְכָל הָעָם עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו מְקוּדָּשׁ מְקוּדָּשׁ.
"The head of the court says, 'It is sanctified,' and all the people answer after him, 'It is sanctified, it is sanctified.'"
וּבְכָל קְדוּשָּׁה יֵשׁ עֶשֶׂר מַדְרֵיגוֹת,
And in every holiness there are ten levels,
וְלָזֶה נִצְרַךְ עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים לְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּכָל עֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת,
and for this, ten days were needed to be refined in all ten attributes,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ יוּכְלוּ לִזְכּוֹת לִיקַּח הַפֶּסַח.
and afterward they could merit to take the Pesach lamb.
אַךְ עֲדַיִין לֹא הָיוּ יְכוֹלִים לְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּעֶשֶׂר הַמִּדּוֹת
However, they were still unable to be refined in all ten attributes
כֵּיוָן שֶׁהָיָה קוֹדֶם מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת.
since it was before the Plague of the Firstborn.
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And it is stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' כ"ט.)
שֶׁעֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת הָיָה כְּנֶגֶד עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא,
that the ten plagues corresponded to the ten Sefiros from below to above,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכָּל הַמַּכּוֹת הָיָה נָגוֹף וְרָפוֹא:
meaning that all the plagues were "smiting and healing"
נָגוֹף לְמִצְרַיִם וְרָפוֹא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
smiting for Egypt and healing for Israel, as stated in the holy Zohar
(ibid. 36a),
הַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּכָל מַכָּה יָצְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִקְּלִיפָּה אַחַת וְנִתְבָּרְרוּ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה בְּמִדָּה שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגְדָּהּ
meaning that with each plague Israel emerged from one husk and were refined in holiness in its corresponding attribute
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים).
(as has been explained many times).
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהָיָה קוֹדֶם מַכָּה עֲשִׂירִית,
And since it was prior to the tenth plague,
הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּקָּפִין עוֹד בִּקְלִיפָּה עֲשִׂירִית
Israel were still surrounded by the tenth husk
וְלֹא הָיוּ יְכוֹלִים עוֹד לִזְכּוֹת לְקַדֵּשׁ הַפֶּסַח,
and could not yet merit to sanctify the Pesach lamb
רַק מִפְּנֵי שֶׁחָל אָז עָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ בְּשַׁבָּת,
except that because the tenth of the month fell on Shabbos then,
עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת זָכוּ לְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּמִדָּה עֲשִׂירִית, כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן,
through the holiness of Shabbos they merited to be refined in the tenth attribute, Kesser Elyon,
וְיָכְלוּ לְהַשִּׂיג קְדוּשַּׁת הַפֶּסַח.
and were able to attain the holiness of the Pesach offering.
וְאַף שֶׁעֲדַיִין לֹא נִצְטַוּוּ עַל הַשַּׁבָּת,
And even though they had not yet been commanded concerning Shabbos,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת קְבִיעָא וְקַיְימָא מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ,
nevertheless the holiness of Shabbos is fixed and enduring from Hashem, may He be blessed,
כִּדְאִיתָא בִּפְסָחִים
as stated in Pesachim
שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ קָרָא לְשַׁבָּת קֹדֶשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
that Hashem, may He be blessed, called Shabbos holy, as it is said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית ב', ג'):
(Bereishis 2:3):
וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אֹתוֹ.
"And He sanctified it."
וְכָל עִיקַּר הַכֹּחַ שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשִׁין לַמּוֹעֲדוֹת
And the entire foundational power by which Israel sanctify the festivals
הוּא עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁזּוֹכִין יִשְׂרָאֵל,
is through the holiness of Shabbos that Israel merit,
וְשׁוּב עַל יְדֵי זֶה יְכוֹלִין לַעֲשׂוֹת מִקְרָא קֹדֶשׁ.
and subsequently through this they are able to make a "holy convocation."
וּפֶסַח הָיָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁקִּדְּשׁוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And Pesach was the very first festival that Israel sanctified,
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: תְּחִלָּה לְמִקְרָאֵי קֹדֶשׁ זֵכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרָיִם.
and this is what we say: "the first of the holy convocations, a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt."
וּבַתִּיקּוּנִים
And in Tikkunei Zohar
(תִּיקּוּן ל"ו):
(Tikkun 36):
יְהִי אוֹר — דָּא פֶּסַח, אוֹר לְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר וְכוּלֵּי.
"'Let there be light'—this is Pesach, the evening of the fourteenth, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז הִתְחִיל הָאוֹר שֶׁזָּכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִקְדוּשָּׁה.
That is, then began the light through which Israel merited holiness.
וּמַה שֶּׁהָיָה כֹּחַ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לִקְרוֹא לְפֶסַח קֹדֶשׁ בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהָיָה מִקָּחוֹ מִבְּעָשׂוֹר,
And the fact that Israel had the power to proclaim Pesach holy at the Exodus from Egypt—when its acquisition was from the tenth
הָיָה גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁחָל אָז בְּשַׁבָּת כָּאָמוּר.
was also due to the holiness of Shabbos, which fell on Shabbos then, as stated.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי קְרָאוּ שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל,
And therefore they called it Shabbos HaGadol,
דִּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת גָּרַם שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לִקְרוֹא קֹדֶשׁ.
for the holiness of Shabbos enabled Israel to proclaim holiness.
וְאַף שֶׁאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם גַּם כֵּן מַקְדִּישִׁין נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
And even though the nations of the world can also consecrate vows and freewill offerings like Israel,
הוּא גַּם כֵּן רַק מִצַּד קְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
that too is only by virtue of Israel's holiness;
אֲבָל לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת אֵין שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִקְדוּשָּׁה,
for idolaters themselves have no intrinsic connection to holiness,
שֶׁעִיקַּר הַקְּדוּשָּׁה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים,
as the essence of holiness comes through Israel being holy,
וְלָזֶה זָכוּ אָז עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת וְכָאָמוּר.
and this they merited then through the holiness of Shabbos, as stated.

Therefore He killed all the firstborn in Egypt, for that is the highest grade and the firstborn of all." The plagues climbed grade by grade from below to above.

What is the healing? That those who had been circumcised needed healing."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, First Day of Pesach 15 — “Therefore the taking on the tenth fell then on Shabbos, for through Shabbos the refinement is completed in full perfection, even to human eyes. On Shabbos everything is raised to its root; from that ascent the idolaters draw greater darkness and unrestrained excess, but to Israel there is drawn from that same ascent added holiness, the extra soul. Therefore the taking was on the tenth on Shabbos specifically, to make the difference between flock and flock clear to all.” Connection: The same claim that the Shabbos of the tenth made Israel fit to take the Pesach lamb; it locates this in Shabbos openly separating Israel's flock from Egypt's.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 117b — Rava to the elders of Pumbedisa: "Your reason: Shabbos is fixed and established [keviya v'kayma], so in both prayer and kiddush one says 'Who sanctifies the Shabbos'; Yom Tov — Israel fix it, for they intercalate months and set years, so one says 'Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons.'" (On this chapter the commentary is Rashbam, not Rashi.)

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Aharon of Karlin (the Second), Beis Aharon, Shabbos HaGadol — “The Shabbos is great, for every festival has the Shabbos before it, from which the holiness of the festival is drawn. Shabbos is higher in rank than the festival, for the festival is bound to time and Shabbos is not bound to time. Of Shabbos it is written, ‘You shall keep the Shabbos, for it is holy to you’: Shabbos itself is called holy. But of the festival it is written, ‘holy convocations,’ for we call and bring the holiness of Shabbos into the festival; the Shabbos is the preparation for the festival.” Connection: Beis Aharon shares the claim that the holiness Israel proclaims on a festival is drawn from Shabbos, whose holiness is fixed from Above, and he reads the Torah's wording, Shabbos as simply holy and the festivals as convocations Israel call, as the textual sign of that dependence.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bo 9 — “The festivals are called holy convocations because Israel give holiness to them; and Shabbos too, though its holiness is fixed, is called a holy convocation, for on it too the Jew must bring in holiness. And the main holiness a Jew can bring in is only through the Exodus, for before it holiness is mentioned only of Shabbos; only in this parashah, ‘This month shall be for you,’ was Israel given the power to bring holiness into the month.” Connection: Explaining “the first of the holy convocations, a remembrance of the Exodus,” the same contrast between Shabbos sanctified by Hashem and festivals sanctified by Israel; Bo 9 adds that only from the Exodus could Israel bring holiness even into Shabbos.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 36 (77b) — "'Let there be light' — this is Pesach, the night [or] of the fourteenth; 'and there was light' — Rosh Hashanah, of which it is said 'and it was [vayehi] the day'; here vayehi and there vayehi, and everywhere vayehi is a term of distress." Or l'arba'ah asar is the Mishnah's term for the night of the fourteenth (Pesachim 2a).
